Helena V: Heads-up: PR #1674 landed a new section on quant calibration profiles and batch heuristics but I noticed two issues in the published snippets — the Java example still calls `client.setBatchHint()` (deprecated) and the TypeScript example references `/opt/quant-calibrate/latest` which 404s from the public site. Also the calibration note about seed reproducibility is missing.

Tor B: Ack. I saw the Java compile warning in the snippet test. We should switch to the new builder API `BatchConfig.builder().maxSize(64).build()` and add a one-line comment that this is a conservative default.

Samir N: For the TS link, prefer using the canonical alias `https://docs.redwood.ai/quant-calibrate/stable` so bookmarks don't break when we move files around. For reproducibility, add a small note: "set `calibration.seed` when running offline sweeps" and show the env var approach.

Helena V: Proposed patch: 1) change Java snippet to builder API + comment, 2) swap TS link to stable alias, 3) add a short reproducibility note and a tiny script showing `CALIB_SEED=42` usage, 4) include a quick diagnostic curl to confirm calibration metadata is attached to model artifacts.

Tor B: I'll patch the Java snippet. Quick code change:
```java
// conservative quickstart batch config
BatchConfig cfg = BatchConfig.builder().maxSize(64).build();
client.updateBatchConfig(cfg);
```
and add `// tune per workload` comment.

Samir N: I'll update the TS example and the link. For the reproducibility script I suggest we add this pseudo-shell snippet: 
```bash
# run offline calibration with deterministic seed
export CALIB_SEED=42
./calibrate --model rwd-opt-13b --out ./calib-artifacts --seed $CALIB_SEED
```
Add a note: "Deterministic seeds help reproducibility but do not guarantee identical perf across hardware variants."

Clara J: From CS: customers reported that after calibration their latency distribution became bimodal when batching used token-based heuristics. Can we add a short troubleshooting sub-section: check tokenization changes, compare median vs p95, and fall back to size-based batching if bimodal?

Helena V: Good catch. I'll add troubleshooting bullets and a minimal diagnostic to compare token counts pre/post calibration. Something like:
```bash
# tokenization check (pseudo)
echo "<long prefix>" | tokenizer --model rwd-opt-13b | wc -w
echo "<long prefix>" | tokenizer --model rwd-opt-13b-calibrated | wc -w
```
If counts differ significantly, recommend switching to `batchConfig.maxTokens` rather than `maxSize`.
